newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya calm on national strike day.
newsitem.headline: Kenya calm on national strike day.

text.p: The Kenyan capital Nairobi was calm on Friday the day on which opposition groups demanding pre-election political reforms from the government have called for a national strike.

Traffic on Nairobi's usually chaotic streets was thin although many people still managed to get into the city for work because some bus owners ignored the strike call, branded as illegal by the embattled government of President Daniel arap Moi. Most city centre shops, mainly owned by the Asian community, were expected to remain closed because business leaders feared a repeat of the violence and looting which usually mars political protests in the East Africa country.

The political climate has degenerated steadily in the past two months and at least nine people were killed on July 7 in clashes between police and pro-reform demonstrators in Nairobi and other centres.
Organisers of the national strike have scheduled protest rallies on Friday in Nairobi's central Uhuru park and in 11 provincial towns in the country of nearly 30 million people.
